newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSTANT VIEW-Mexico strong industrial production.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Mexico strong industrial production.

text.p: Stronger than expected industrial production data for May lifted Mexico's stock market and may boost second quarter economic growth, analysts said on Tuesday.
May industrial production rose 9.0 percent compared with the same month last year. A Reuter survey of 12 analysts forecasts showed an average expectation of 7.88 percent.
SERGIO MARTIN, MEXICO ECONOMIST, ING BARINGS
"The figure came in above the consensus expectation. It looks like the second quarter in general will be very strong -- stronger than people thought."
"Once we get the June figures, we could reach a 10 percent average for industrial production for the whole quarter, and we could get second quarter GDP of five to six percent at least."

He said Santander had been bearish on the output number, expecting it to rise just 5.5 percent. Ramirez said he would now raise his Q2 GDP forecast from 5 percent to 5.4 or 5.5 percent, which he said would be a good number because it compares with a fairly strong quarter last year.
"It could be due to recovery inertia, and it could also be partly at least due to the fact this has been an electoral quarter, with increased spending by the government in general," he said.
"The nine percent increase is very positive. It suggests that Q2 GDP should be strong."
